outcome: Fetal outcomes (umbilical cord c-peptide levels, neonatal hypoglycaemia, perinatal mortality, preterm birth)
cohort: 2917 pregnant women in five major hospitals in urban/semi-urban central Uganda
finding: HIP, particularly DIP, was associated with significant adverse pregnancy outcomes, including large birthweight, Caesarean delivery, and neonatal hypoglycaemia, highlighting the need for improved monitoring and management of HIP in this population.
mod_finding: HIP was associated with Caesarean delivery (RR 1.34, 95% CI 1.14-1.57).
gest_age: 24-28 weeks at time of OGTT screening
birth_weight: Large birthweight was more common in babies born to mothers with HIP
